asparagus-frozen-cooked-with-butter-or-m.title: Asparagus, frozen, cooked with butter or margarine

content.title: About
content.content: Asparagus is the edible shoot of the plant Asparagus officinalis. Frozen asparagus cooked with butter or margarine is a ready‑to‑eat product that retains most of its nutrients and its characteristic tender flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Asparagus is one of the oldest cultivated vegetables, grown for over 2,000 years.
Freezing preserves its bright green color and crisp texture.
Cooking with butter or margarine enhances the absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins such as vitamin K.
Asparagus contains aromatic compounds that become more pronounced with a light sauté in butter.
In the United States, frozen cooked asparagus is often sold as a convenient side dish.

items.title: Rich in vitamin K
items.content: Vitamin K is essential for blood clotting and bone health.

items.title: Contains folate
items.content: Folate supports DNA synthesis and is especially important during pregnancy.

items.title: Low‑calorie food
items.content: A serving provides few calories, making it suitable for weight‑management diets.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Asparagus supplies vitamin C, glutathione, and other antioxidants that protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber promotes digestive health and helps maintain a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to asparagus.

items.title: Oxalate content
items.content: Asparagus contains oxalates, which can contribute to kidney stone formation in susceptible people.

items.title: Fat content
items.content: Cooking with butter or margarine adds calories and fat; those monitoring fat intake should consider portion size.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Heat the frozen asparagus in a skillet or microwave, adding a pat of butter or margarine. Serve as a side dish with meat, fish, or incorporate into salads. Season with garlic, lemon juice, or your favorite herbs.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the frozen product in a freezer at –18 °C (0 °F). Once thawed, use within 1–2 days and do not re‑freeze; discard if it develops an off odor or texture.

content.title: About
content.content: Beef and noodles, no sauce is a simple dish consisting of boiled noodles and tender pieces of beef cooked by steaming or dry‑frying without any added sauce. It is ideal for a quick lunch or dinner when a hearty, neutral‑flavored meal is desired.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The dish is often served in school cafeterias and canteens because it contains no allergenic sauces.
The noodles are usually wheat‑based but can be swapped for rice or buckwheat noodles for a gluten‑free version.
Serving beef without sauce preserves the natural meat flavor, making it popular among fans of “clean” cuisine.
Traditionally prepared in Asian countries where noodles and meat are frequently served separately.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Beef provides high‑quality animal protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Iron and zinc
items.content: Red meat is a good source of easily absorbed iron and zinc, supporting immune function.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Beef supplies vitamin B12, niacin, and riboflavin, important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Carbohydrates from noodles
items.content: Noodles deliver quick‑digesting carbs that give energy for an active day.

items.title: Low sugar content
items.content: The absence of sauce means the dish contains virtually no added sugars, beneficial for blood‑glucose control.

items.title: High saturated fat content
items.content: Beef can contain saturated fats; choose lean cuts and consume in moderation.

items.title: Sodium levels
items.content: If the noodles are pre‑salted, sodium may be high; opt for unsalted noodles when possible.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Traditional wheat noodles contain gluten, making the dish unsuitable for people with celiac disease.

items.title: Thorough cooking required
items.content: Beef should be cooked to a safe internal temperature to avoid food‑borne illness.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the dish hot, seasoning with salt, pepper, or fresh herbs to taste. It pairs well with vegetable sides, a green salad, or a light broth.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the prepared dish in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. When frozen, it retains quality for up to 2 months. Reheat thoroughly before eating to prevent bacterial growth.

content.title: About
content.content: The Double Cheeseburger is a classic fast‑food item featuring two large beef patties (169 g each), two slices of cheese, fresh vegetables, sauce, and a sesame‑seed bun. It combines juicy meat with melted cheese for a rich, satisfying flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first double cheeseburger appeared in the United States in the 1970s as a response to growing demand for heartier burgers.
Each patty weighs about 169 g, giving the burger a total meat weight of over 350 g before the bun and toppings.
The double layer of cheese boosts calcium content to roughly 200 mg per serving.
It is often served with fries and a soft drink as a “combo” meal.
Some locations offer variations with bacon or fried onions.

items.title: Protein
items.content: Two beef patties provide approximately 40 g of protein, essential for muscle repair and growth.

items.title: Calcium
items.content: Cheese adds a good source of calcium, supporting bone health.

items.title: Iron
items.content: Beef is rich in heme iron, which is readily absorbed by the body.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The meat supplies vitamin B12 and niacin, important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Energy
items.content: The combination of protein, fat, and carbs provides a quick energy boost.

items.title: High Calorie Content
items.content: A double cheeseburger can contain over 800 kcal, which may contribute to weight gain if eaten frequently.

items.title: Saturated Fat and Sodium
items.content: The cheese and sauce increase saturated fat and salt levels, which can affect cardiovascular health.

items.title: Dairy Allergy
items.content: Cheese may trigger allergic reactions in people with lactose intolerance or milk protein allergy.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: The bun contains wheat, making the product unsuitable for a gluten‑free diet.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The burger is typically served in a split bun, making it easy to hold. It can be enjoyed with fries, barbecue sauce, or a spicy sauce of your choice.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Best consumed immediately. If needed, store in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours, wrapped tightly to retain moisture. Reheat in an oven or on a grill rather than a microwave to keep the bun’s texture.

egg-white-omelet-scrambled-or-fried-made.title: Egg White Omelet, Scrambled or Fried with Butter

content.title: About
content.content: Egg white omelet, scrambled or fried with butter is a dish made from pure egg whites cooked in butter. Egg whites provide high‑quality protein with virtually no fat or carbs, while butter adds a rich flavor and aroma.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Egg whites contain almost all essential amino acids.
Cooking in butter enhances absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins such as vitamin D.
Egg white protein is highly digestible, making it popular among athletes.
Butter gives a distinctive taste that is hard to replicate with other fats.
Egg white omelets are often used in diet plans because of their low calorie density.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Egg whites provide about 10 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Low in fat and carbohydrates
items.content: 100 g of egg whites contain virtually no fat or carbs, suitable for low‑carb diets.

items.title: Contains vitamin B2 (riboflavin)
items.content: Riboflavin is involved in energy metabolism and supports healthy skin and eyes.

items.title: Supports immune function
items.content: Proteins and selenium in egg whites help maintain a normal immune response.

items.title: Easily digestible
items.content: Egg white protein is quickly absorbed, making it ideal post‑workout.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to egg whites, ranging from skin rashes to anaphylaxis.

items.title: High cholesterol in butter
items.content: Butter contains saturated fat and cholesterol; excessive use may raise LDL levels.

items.title: Risk of foodborne illness
items.content: Using non‑fresh eggs can lead to salmonella contamination.

items.title: Low vitamin D content
items.content: Egg whites contain little vitamin D, so additional sources are needed for adequate intake.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Whisk egg whites, add a pinch of salt and optional herbs. Melt butter in a skillet over medium heat, pour the mixture, and cook to the desired consistency—from soft scrambled to firm omelet. Serve with vegetables, herbs, or a sprinkle of low‑fat cheese.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the cooked omelet in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. Raw egg whites should be kept refrigerated in their original packaging and used within 3–5 days.

fruit-juice-drink-added-calcium-sunny-d.title: Sunny D – Fruit Juice Drink with Added Calcium

content.title: About
content.content: Sunny D is a non‑alcoholic fruit juice drink fortified with calcium. It is made from orange juice, water, sugar, natural flavorings, and calcium added as an easily absorbable salt. The beverage is marketed as a source of B‑vitamins and bone‑supporting nutrients.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The Sunny D brand was launched in the United States in the 1970s and quickly became popular with children.
Calcium is added as calcium phosphate, which does not alter the taste.
One serving provides more than the daily recommended amount of vitamin C for adults.
The drink is often used in school cafeterias as an alternative to regular juices.
Sunny D’s bright orange color comes from natural carotenoids.

items.title: Bone support
items.content: Added calcium helps maintain bone density, especially important for growing children and teenagers.

items.title: Vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C boosts immunity and participates in collagen synthesis.

items.title: Energy boost
items.content: Simple sugars quickly replenish energy stores after physical activity.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: The high water content aids in maintaining proper fluid balance.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Vitamins B2 and B6 support carbohydrate and protein metabolism.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Regular consumption may contribute to weight gain and increase the risk of dental caries.

items.title: Citrus allergy
items.content: People allergic to oranges or other citrus fruits may experience reactions.

items.title: Excess calcium
items.content: Overconsumption can put strain on the kidneys, especially in individuals prone to kidney stones.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: The drink’s acidic pH may irritate a sensitive stomach.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Sunny D is typically served chilled. It can be enjoyed on its own, used in cocktails, smoothies, or diluted with water to reduce sweetness.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep refrigerated and consume within 5‑7 days.

green-peas-canned-reduced-sodium-cooked-.title: Green peas, canned, reduced sodium, cooked, no added fat

content.title: About
content.content: Canned green peas are a fully cooked, ready‑to‑eat product made from fresh pea pods that have been blanched, lightly salted, and sealed in a can. This version contains reduced sodium and no added fat, making it a convenient and healthier option for quick meals.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Green peas belong to the legume family and are an excellent source of plant‑based protein.
Canning preserves most B‑vitamins and minerals despite the heat treatment.
Reduced‑sodium varieties use a milder brine and a brief rinse before sealing to lower salt content.
Peas are a staple in many world cuisines, appearing in soups, purees, salads, and side dishes.
Canned peas have a long shelf life—typically 3 to 5 years when stored in a cool, dry place.

items.title: Rich in plant protein
items.content: One cup of canned peas provides about 8 g of protein, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion, helps regulate blood sugar, and promotes satiety.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Peas contain folate, thiamine, and vitamin B6, which are important for metabolism and nervous system health.

items.title: Contains iron and magnesium
items.content: These minerals contribute to hemoglobin formation and normal muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Reduced sodium
items.content: Lower salt levels make this product suitable for people monitoring blood pressure.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to peas.

items.title: Natural sugars
items.content: Peas are naturally sweet; large portions can add to overall sugar intake.

items.title: Preservatives
items.content: Certain brands may add preservatives; check the label if you are sensitive.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Add peas to soups, stews, salads, mash them into a puree, or serve as a side dish. They can be heated quickly in the microwave or on the stovetop; rinsing before use can further reduce residual salt.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the unopened can in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, transfer leftovers to an airtight container and refrigerate for 3–4 days. Discard if you notice off‑odors or discoloration.

content.title: About
content.content: NFS potato chips are thinly sliced potato pieces that are fried until crisp and seasoned with salt and spices. The product is made from selected potatoes that are peeled, sliced, washed, dried and quickly fried in vegetable oil at high temperature.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first commercial chip brand appeared in the USA in 1853, and NFS is one of the most popular brands in Russia.
NFS chips are available in several flavors: classic, barbecue, sour cream & onion, etc.
To achieve a crunchy texture the potatoes are blanched beforehand, reducing acrylamide formation.
The packaging is multi‑layered to keep the chips crisp and protect them from moisture.
A standard serving (30 g) provides about 150 kcal.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: Potato chips contain carbohydrates that quickly supply energy.

items.title: Vitamin C content
items.content: A small amount of vitamin C is retained during rapid frying, supporting the immune system.

items.title: Potassium
items.content: Potatoes are rich in potassium, important for fluid balance and muscle function.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: A modest amount of fiber contributes to digestive health.

items.title: Pleasurable taste
items.content: The crunch and aroma can improve mood and satisfy snack cravings.

items.title: High salt content
items.content: Chips often contain a lot of sodium, which may raise blood pressure if consumed in excess.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Because of their fat and carbohydrate content, chips are calorie‑dense and can contribute to weight gain.

items.title: Trans fats and acrylamide
items.content: Frying can produce small amounts of trans fats and acrylamide, compounds with potential health concerns.

items.title: Potato allergy
items.content: Rarely, some individuals may be allergic to potatoes or to seasoning additives.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: NFS chips are convenient as a standalone snack, can be added to salads, used in dishes for crunch, and served with dips and sauces.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store chips in the original package or an airtight container in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, consume within 1–2 weeks to maintain crispness.
